question: The Social Service League was founded in Bombay by:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Narayan Malhar Joshi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Narayan Malhar Joshi **was a notable figure in India's social reform movements during the early 20th century.
 
• In 1911, he established the** Social Service League in Bombay** with the noble aim of enhancing the living standards and working conditions of the masses.
 
• The league's primary focus was on gathering and analyzing social data, engaging in discussions on social issues, and shaping public opinion on matters related to social welfare.
 
• Alongside his involvement in the Social Service League, Joshi played pivotal roles in various other organizations dedicated to social and political causes.
 
• He was a prominent member of the Servants of India Society and actively contributed to the People's Volunteer Brigade.
 
• In 1920, Joshi was instrumental in co-founding the All India Trade Union Congress, underscoring his commitment to advocating for workers' rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Narayan Malhar Joshi, **a follower of Gopal Krishna Gokhale, was a prominent Indian trade union leader.
 
• In 1920, Joshi, along with Lala Lajpat Rai, established the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC).
 
• He served as the general secretary of AITUC from 1925 to 1929 and again from 1940 to 1948.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manabendra Nath Roy, **a 20th-century Indian revolutionary, philosopher, and political theorist, founded the Mexican Communist Party and the Communist Party of India (Tashkent group).
 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale, **an Indian political leader and social reformer, played a pivotal role during the Indian independence movement and served as the political mentor of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• **Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade** was a British-era Indian judge, writer, and social reformer.
